text: UI Policies react automatically to field values. This lesson covers UI Actions - configurable buttons, form links, and context-menu items that wait for a deliberate click, like Close All Related Tasks or Escalate, stored on the sys_ui_action table.

A UI Action's own checkboxes decide where it physically appears: as a form button sitting on the record itself, as a list banner button above a whole list, or as a list choice - a right-click context menu item on an individual list row. The same UI Action record can target more than one of those at once.

Before anything else, every UI Action evaluates a Condition field - a small server-side script that must return true for the action to even render. This example checks that the record's state is 6 and that the user holds the itil role, so the button stays hidden from anyone who can't act on it, or when the record isn't ready.

The single most important setting on a UI Action is its Client checkbox. Check it, and the script in the Script field runs directly in the browser with full g_form access - exactly like a button-triggered mini Client Script. This example reads a close_notes field with g_form.getValue, alerts if it's empty, and otherwise submits the form.

Leave Client unchecked, and the script runs server-side instead, after the page posts back, with access to current - the same object Business Rules use. This example checks current.state, updates the record, calls current.update, and then calls action.setRedirectURL, passing it the record to redirect the user back to it once the script finishes.

Choosing between the two lanes mirrors a decision this course has already made once, for Client Scripts versus Business Rules. If the action only needs to read or adjust what's already on the form, keep it client-side and skip the round trip. If it needs to touch the database or guarantee the same behavior no matter who clicks it, it belongs server-side, working against current. Next lesson moves to UI Pages - the older, Jelly-based mechanism for building a standalone custom interface that isn't tied to displaying a single record's form.
